chapter: WWL and the Roosevelt Fountain Lounge
title: Quitting the band over leader pay and joining Pinky's WWL staff orchestra
summary: Frank learns Bill Padron had kept the leader pay, quits, and joins Pinky at WWL; schedule and pay of the staff orchestra.

bands.name: Bill Padron and Frank Netto's band

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Oh, well Bill and I had the band over there and then Bill got sick that, and he went to the hospital. And when they paid me off, Bill, we were splitting the leader price, Bill and I. And when I went to the hospital, and they paid me off that night and they paid me the full salary. And I said to myself, he said, what you looking at? It's so funny. He said, ain't right? He says, ain't that what you been getting all the time? And I didn't say nothing. I said to myself, ain't what I been getting all the time. But Bill came to me a few weeks before that and said that he had a lot of trouble with it, this and that. And he says, they wanted to let us go. And I didn't know anything about it because they wanted to let us go. And he says, we decided we'd let them keep the leader price. And so Bill took the money and paid them off every night and gave it to me. And then he cut my salary down. Where was this? At Hunsuckle Inn, Pete Vetrana. And Pete paid me the whole salary. And it was a leader, you got $52.50, you remember? And the job was $35, and so we split together $17.50. And so Bill went to the hospital, I paid the guys off and I went to him and I said, Bill, I says, you told me that they cut the leader price. Was this guy named Dupre that was a talk about? That was it. That was Jimmy Dupre. Jimmy Dupre. Jimmy Dupre. Jimmy Dupre. That's the guy. So I went to the hospital and I told him over there and I says, you did, I said, why didn't you ask me for the money? I said, for Christ's sake, I'd have gave you the money. I said, he says, well, I didn't want to do this and want to die. I said, well, if that's the way you, you son of a bitch, I hope you die. That's the words I told him. I said, I hope you die. And I quit the orchestra. That's when I told him, I said, you can have the band. And I don't know how long he stayed out there after I did. And then I joined Pinky right after that. And with the WWL staff orchestra. That was the first orchestra. remember Benitez started the first two weeks?
Yeah. Benitez says that he gave Pinky the job.

Benitez and Pinky got the band together. But Benitez wanted to pick out different men in the band. He didn't want this guy and he didn't want that guy. And Pinky told him, I said, now look, Ray. He says, I'm the leader of the band. And Larry said, if you're going to handle the band, he says, go ahead and take it. He says, I quit. So Ray quit. He played two weeks up there. So Pinky phoned me and told him, he says, you want to come on up? He says, I got a job over here. I says, I'll take it. Was Ray playing bass then? Yeah, he played bass. He opened up the WWL staff orchestra for the first two weeks. What year was that? Huh? What year was that? Well, before the banks closed, because we stayed up there for about two years, and then the banks closed. Wasn't the banks closed? About 30, 40, right?

Yeah. So we started in there around 32. And we played up there three sessions a day. 8 to 8.30, 11.30 to 12, and 4.15 to 5.15. What was the band called? The WWL Staff Orchestra. That's all. That's the same. Under the direction of Pinky Repolkovich, where we played nothing but stuff. And our salary was $25 a week. At least.
